Preparation of Lung Tissue Blocks for MPLEx
Place the sample in the cryostat (allow to thermally equilibrate ~20 min)
Cut 2x sections (50 μm) and place sections in pre-weighed 2 mL Sorenson MµlTI™ SafeSeal™ Microcentrifuge Tubes VWR International (Avantor) Catalog #53550
Use a Rapid-Core Sampling Punch - 4 mm Ted Pella Inc. Catalog #15115-10 to punch 2 tissue cores from each tissue section and place the punches in pre-weighed 2 mL Sorenson MµlTI™ SafeSeal™ Microcentrifuge Tubes VWR International (Avantor) Catalog #53550 *Note: When punching the tissue cores, avoid regions with OCT, as this can be difficult to remove from the sample and may yield contamination within the mass spectrum.

Synaptic vesicle preparation from mouse brain
Centrifuge homogenate at 871 × g, 10 min, 4°C. Collect the supernatant (S1).
Resuspend the LP2 pellet in SHT buffer diluted to 40 mM sucrose (prepared by diluting standard SHT buffer: 0.3 M sucrose, 1 mM Mg-EGTA, 10 mM HEPES-Tris, pH 7.4).
Prepare a 5–25% glycerol gradient using the glycerol gradient buffer using a gradient maker to form a continuous gradient.

text:
ARISE Fungi DNA Extraction
Note: For high throughput, DNA extraction in plates can be automated using a purification instrument (e.g. a ThermoFisher Scientific KingFisher Flex or a MolGen PurePrep 96) or a liquid handling platform. Binding Centrifuge the incubated samples down for 5 minutes at max centrifuge speed at room temperature to pellet solid particles at the bottom of the plate / tube. Transfer 75 µl of the supernatant to a deep well plate / tube. Add 20 µl SeraSil-Mag 400 beads to each sample (make sure the beads are properly shaken into suspension before adding to the samples). Add 150 μl (2x the lysate volume) of Tissue Binding Buffer to each sample. Incubate 5 minutes at room temperature on a shaker.
Tissue Binding Buffer (per 100 ml) Dissolve 26.3 g guanidine hydrochloride in 20 ml milliQ. Stir until dissolved. Adjust the volume to 50 ml with milliQ. Add 50 ml 100% ethanol.
2% CTAB pH8 (per 100 ml) Combine 10 ml 1 M Tris pH 8.0, 4 ml 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0, 28.4 ml 5M NaCl and 2 g CTAB. Add MilliQ water to a volume of 60 ml and heat in a water bath until CTAB is dissolved. Bring the total volume to 100 ml with milliQ. Ready-to-use CTAB buffer can also be purchased commercially.

text:
OceanOmics Centre: 12S, 16S and COI Metabarcoding of Marine Vertebrates
In the attached Input_Template, enter all required samples in the Metadata tab and assign each one to its corresponding project. Do not edit any other tab, these contain the primer and index sequences for all assays. Input_Template.xlsx NOTES: Index combinations can only be used once per assay within a single sequencing run. Reusing an index combination on the same run will cause sample reads to be mixed together and cannot be demultiplexed. Sequencing runs must therefore be planned before qPCR to ensure no index combinations overlap. Target read depth must also be defined in advance, based on the number of samples going onto the run, to ensure the sequencing run capacity is filled appropriately.
Using the Echo Software, survey the plates, ensuring that the volume in each well is between 12 µL and 65 µL. If the value is too low, prepare a new plate, if the value is too high, there may be air bubbles or droplets on the plate. Spin-down and survey again. NOTES: Wipe the bottom of the plates with a Kimwipe before loading onto the Echo. See Echo 525 manual for detailed instructions on how to survey plates and run protocols.
Run the run_meta_to_plates script. This will create a template of your eDNA samples, in both 96-well and 384-well plate layouts, as well the layout of the tagged primers. As a default, the template will reserve the bottom right two quadrants of the plate for the NTC (negative control) and ITC (positive control). Samples are placed in triplicate reactions in positions 1-3 of each quadrant of the plate as per the image below. The 4th well is reserved for pooling the triplicate reactions.

text:
CosMx Spatial Transcriptomics Protocol
Cut the samples at 5 µM and center the sections in the green scan area. Bake the slides Overnight at 37 °C and store them at 4 °C until you use them. [Use within 2 weeks for best results]. Slide prep follows the guidelines given by Nanostring : CosMx SMI Manual Slide Preparation for RNA Assays.
Hybridization (Overnight) If timing is off, store slides in 2X SSC wash for 01:00:00 at Room temperature or up to 06:00:00 at 4 °C . Ensure Buffer R is at Room temperature before opening. Prepare a 1:10 dilution of the probe (~15μL/slide) and mix by pipetting 3-5 times (Do not vortex). Preheat the thermal cycler and lid to 95 °C . Remove the incubation frame cover and clean it with ethanol. Lay it on a Kimwipe until ready for use. Flick probes and use a mini centrifuge before applying.
Target-Level QC Flags genes with expression levels potentially below background. oNegative control probe quantile cutoff (default: 0.5, range 0-1): Flags probes with lower counts than the median of negative control probes. oDetection p-value (default: 0.01, range 0-1): Determines whether a target gene is above background. Lower p-value = More stringent filtering. Higher p-value = More relaxed filtering.
